summary: Anantasharma B. G. is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned degrees from National Sanskrit University, University of Madras, SVYASA, and Central Sanskrit University (PhD 2021). Posts include Head at Veda Vijnana Shodha Samsthana, Chairperson at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, and Assistant Professor at Chanakya University.

Ananya Vajpeyi works in Indology, philosophy, and history/archaeology. She studied at University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, University of Oxford, Exeter College, and University of Chicago (PhD 2004). She held posts at Columbia University and the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies.

Anastasiya Lozhkina specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Moscow State University, becoming a Junior Research Fellow at the Russian Academy of Sciences in 2018.

Anatol Waag studied linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies at the University of Leipzig under Johannes Hertel, earning his PhD around 1931. He served as an assistant at Leipzig (1932–1939) and lectured in German at the University of Zagreb (~1937–1941).
Anatoli Guenko studied under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay and Boris Turayev around 1914 to 1918.
Anders Hilding Andersson was an Indology scholar who earned his MA and PhD (~1878) at Lund University. In 1879, he became Docent of Greek Literature at Lund University.

Andrea Acri is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Raffaele Torella, Willem van der Molen, and Arlo Griffiths at Leiden University (PhD ~2011). His appointments include Assistant Professor at EPHE and Adjunct Researcher at EFEO (2021–2024).

Andrea R. Jain is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Southern Methodist University and Rice University (PhD 2010). She held appointments at the University of Houston, Rice University, IUPUI, and Indiana University Bloomington, where she became full professor in 2021.

Andrea Schlosser specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies, earning her MA and PhD (2014) at Free University of Berlin and studying under Richard G. Salomon and Ingo Strauch. She held research posts at the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Andreas Bock-Raming studied under Paul Hacker and works in the fields of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held a research post at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Andreas Doctor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completing his PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura alongside multiple traditional teachers. He held a post at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Andreas Gottlieb Hoffmann worked in religious studies and linguistics, earning his PhD at Halle-Wittenberg under Wilhelm Gesenius. He served as Privatdozent at Halle-Wittenberg (1822) and became Professor of Theology at the University of Jena in 1826.
Andreas N. Kephallenos was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who completed his education at the University of Florence and the University of Munich, where he earned a PhD.
Andreas Spengel was a scholar in linguistics who studied at the University of Munich (~1856–1858) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1858–1860). He taught Albert Grünwedel.
Andree Dominique Messent specializes in Buddhist studies. Messent earned a PhD at the University of Bristol under doctoral supervisor Paul Williams, also studying with Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.

Andrei Vostrikov worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, studying at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Boris Vladimirtsov. He held researcher posts at the Asiatic Museum and Institute of Buddhist Culture, and taught at the Leningrad Institute of Living Oriental Languages.

Andrej Evgen’evič Snesarev worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. After studying at Moscow State University and the General Staff Academy, he headed the General Staff Academy (1919) and served as Rector of the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1922–1924).
Andrew B. Irvine is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a PhD from Boston University. He served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College (attested 2009).
Andrew Garrett is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who completed his PhD at Harvard University around 1990. In 1995, he became a professor at the University of California, Berkeley.

Andrew Glass works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Washington, completing his MA and PhD (2006) under Richard G. Salomon, while also studying with Mark Allon, Ulrich Pagel, Sonam Wanggyal, and Gudrun Melzer.
